items.title: Bias vs. Variance — Without the Bullseye
items.summary:
Bias and variance are two of the most important ideas in machine learning — but you don’t need the classic bullseye diagram to understand them.

In this short, Luis Serrano, author of Grokking Machine Learning, Second Edition, explains the relationship between bias and variance in a simple, intuitive way, helping beginners see how models can be too simple, too sensitive, or just right.

A clear explanation for anyone learning how machine learning models make mistakes.

Book: https://hubs.la/Q04rsqf30

#MachineLearning #AI #BiasVariance #DataScience #LearnAI #Python #ManningBooks #LuisSerrano

items.title: Did This AI Company Go Too Far...?
items.summary:
Friend 2.0 might be the weirdest AI product launch I’ve seen all year 😭

The AI necklace can now talk back to you, and somehow the ad they made for it raises even more questions than the product itself.

The founder has described Friend as a kind of “confidant, friend, God,” says the first 5,000 devices sold out, and now wants to sell 50,000 of these.

And there are clearly people who genuinely want this. One commenter on X even said AI makes a better counselor than therapy.

So… am I being old-fashioned, or is this where we’re actually headed?

#AI #aitech #ainews

items.title: Lines Of Code Was Never The Metric
items.summary: In episode 1017 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, @JonKrohnLearns talks with Pete Johnson, Field CTO at MongoDB, about the critical lessons learned from 'token maxing' at companies like Uber. Pete explains how tracking vanity metrics such as lines of code or token consumption led to massive inefficiencies and cost overruns, emphasizing that true AI productivity should be measured by business outcomes like faster software delivery cycles, not output volume.

items.title: Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max: Open-Weight Model Surpasses Most American Frontier Labs (Ep. 1018)
items.summary:
In Episode #1018, @JonKrohnLearns breaks down Qwen3.8-Max, Alibaba’s enormous new flagship, a 2.4-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that, if its promised weights ship, becomes the largest open-weight release in history. Landing just weeks after Moonshot’s Kimi K3, it extends the price war and the open-weight surge Jon covered in Episode #1012. Alibaba positions it as second only to Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 / Mythos 5 and independent signals land in a similar neighborhood. Jon walks through its capabilities and multi-day agentic demos, its aggressive pricing ($2 in / $6 out per million tokens, with cached input eight times cheaper), and the question he gets asked most: are Chinese models safe to use? His answer hinges far less on the model than on how your data reach it.

Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1018
